test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 04 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated in the Union Territory of Ladakh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Yuru Kabgyat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Yuru Kabgyat** is one of the most significant monastic festivals celebrated in the **Union Territory of Ladakh**.
 
• The festival takes place at the **Lamayuru Monastery**, which is also known as **Yuru Gompa**, located about **127 km** from **Leh**.
 
• It is a **two-day** annual event held during the **second month** of the **Tibetan lunar calendar**, typically falling in the months of **June** or **July**.
 
• The festival is dedicated to **Guru Padmasambhava** (the Second Buddha) and **Yamanthaka** (the deity of death), aimed at seeking protection from natural calamities and bringing peace to the world.
 
• The central attraction of the festival is the **Cham Dance**, a sacred masked dance performed by the **Buddhist monks** to the accompaniment of traditional music played with drums, cymbals, and long pipes.
 
• The masks used in the **Cham Dance** represent various guardian deities and mythological figures, and the performance symbolizes the **victory of good over evil**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Karaga**:

 
 
• It is one of the oldest and most important folk festivals of **Karnataka**, specifically celebrated in **Bengaluru**.
 
• The festival is dedicated to **Draupadi**, the wife of the Pandavas, and is celebrated by the **Tigala** community during the **Chaitra** month (March/April).
 
 
 
• **Shigmo**:
 
 
• Also known as **Shishirotsava**, it is the largest spring festival celebrated in the state of **Goa**.
 
• It is a vibrant celebration by the Hindu community involving street dances, traditional folk songs, and colorful floats, marking the arrival of spring and the homecoming of warriors.
 
 
 
• **Thrissur Pooram**:
 
 
• It is considered the "festival of festivals" in **Kerala**, held at the **Vadakkunnathan Temple** in **Thrissur**.
 
• Introduced by **Sakthan Thampuran** (the Maharaja of Cochin) in the year **1797**, it is famous for its grand procession of decorated elephants and spectacular fireworks display.
 
 
 
• **Other Festivals of Ladakh**:
 
 
• **Hemis Festival**: Celebrated at the **Hemis Monastery** to commemorate the birth anniversary of **Guru Padmasambhava**.
 
• **Losar**: This is the **Tibetan New Year**, celebrated with great fervor across the **Union Territory** for about **15 days**.
 
• **Dosmoche**: Known as the "Festival of Scapegoats," it is celebrated in **Leh**, **Likir**, and **Diskit** monasteries to drive away evil spirits.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lamayuru Monastery**, the venue for **Yuru Kabgyat**, is one of the oldest and largest monasteries in **Ladakh**, often referred to as **"Moonland"** due to its unique lunar-like landscape.
 
• The **Union Territory of Ladakh** was established on **31st October 2019**, following the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act** passed by the **Parliament of India**.
 
• The **Cham Dance** performed during these festivals is intended as a form of **meditation** and an offering to the deities, showcasing the rich **Indo-Tibetan** cultural heritage of the region.
 
• Specific musical instruments like the **Dungchen** (long copper trumpets) are integral to the ritualistic atmosphere of **Ladakhi** monastic festivals.
